newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA NATIONAL CAR PROJECT GETS $650 MLN LOAN.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA NATIONAL CAR PROJECT GETS $650 MLN LOAN.

text.p: A consortium of 16 Indonesian banks have agreed to disburse $650 million in 10-year loans to PT Timor Putra Nasional, controlled by President Suharto's son Hutomo Mandala Putra, to finance the national car project, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Tuesday.
Apart from the $650 milllion in loans, state-owned Bank Dagang Negara (BDN), as the consortium leader, had earlier disbursed $40 million in bridging finance to Timor, it said.
Members of the consortium include four state banks -- BDN, Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI), Bank Ekspor Impor Indonesia (Exim) and Bank Tabungan Negara (BTN).
The rest include 12 private banks whose names were not disclosed.

"We hope the agreement on the loan facility will be signed this month," Mandala Putra was quoted as saying by the Jakarta Post. He had earlier asked for a package of $690 million in loans to help finance the car project, including the construction of automobile manufacturing facilities in Cikampek, West Java.
The government last year granted tax and tariff breaks to Timor Putra to jointly produce the national car in collaboration with Kia Motors Corp of South Korea.
Japan, the United States and the European Union have complained against the move, saying it discriminates afainst existing car makers and have brought the case before the world Trade Organisation.
